newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end weak, off lows on bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end weak, off lows on bargain-hunting.

text.p: Malaysian share prices staged a partial recovery on Friday afternoon as late bargain-hunting by large local funds pulled the key index off its earlier lows, dealers said.
The benchmark Composite Index closed 2.54 points, or 0.25 percent, down at 1,001.55, after having dipped to a low of 990.22. The small-capitalised Second Board index gained 1.17 points to 527.80
"Some large local funds have been in the market bargain hunting," said a dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage.
Tenaga and Telekom both hit year lows.
Continuing weakness in the ringgit kept genuine share investors on the sidelines, said analysts.
Lingering uncertainty over the $6.18 billion Bakun hydroelectric dam project continued to prey on investors' minds, they added.
"The fact that it may be delayed has made people more sceptical about the project, and its possible repercussions for the country," said Faez Khairuddin, head of research at SJ Securities.
Bakun project leader Ekran rose two cents to 4.80 ringgit.
